$comment: Each case names a fixture that validates CLEAN, the rule it sits one edit away from, and the edit that removes the refuting evidence. The gate applies the edit to a copy and requires the validator to reject it for that reason. A case that does not flip means the rule never fires, and the fixture's cleanliness was never evidence of anything.
$comment_why_a_floor: A refutation case is deleted the same way a negative proof is: by removing the line, after which every gate stays green. The floor makes the deletion an edit a reviewer sees, in a file under scripts/gates/** and therefore protected.

cases.removes: the `-legacy` suffix that puts F-004 outside the declared `not_read` surface
cases.why: `migrations-legacy/` starts with the six letters of `migrations` and is a different directory. A prefix match would convict this finding; the rule matches at a path segment boundary, so it does not.

cases.removes: the redaction marker in F-002's evidence
cases.needle: an unredacted secret format appears in the artifact
cases.why: The evidence field of a real finding quotes the thing that was found. The rule has to read the redaction and not the shape of the line around it.

edit.old: "inference": "Whether the packaged build enforces OS code signing was not observed: the signed artifact was not available.",

cases.needle: `probable` must name the link that was inferred
cases.why: A `probable` finding is the shape most likely to be over-claimed, and this artifact carries three statuses. The rule may not fire on the two that are not `probable`.

edit.old:
,
      "what_would_settle_it": "The session middleware in `app/middleware/session.js`, which is not in the delivered scope and decides whether the token is re-verified per request."

cases.needle: `probable` must say what would settle it
cases.why: The second half of the same doctrine, and a separate rule: naming the inference is not naming the artifact that would end the argument.

cases.removes: the reason attached to F-002's `UNKNOWN` triage answer

edit.old:
"answer": "UNKNOWN",
          "reason": "The notarization setting lives in the release pipeline, which is outside the audited repository; asked for the pipeline export."

cases.why: `UNKNOWN` is this project's third state inside triage. An answer of UNKNOWN with a reason is the correct use; the rule must not treat the state itself as the defect.

"reason": "the variable is a table name taken from a hardcoded tuple in the same module, and the migration runner is never reached with request data; the second reading overturned the first",

edit.new: "reason": "the variable is a table name taken from a hardcoded tuple in the same module, and the migration runner is never reached with request data; the second reading overturned the first"

cases.why: Dropping a candidate is the edit that makes a report look clean. Dropping one WITH the line that refutes it is the behaviour being asked for, and it has to pass.

cases.removes: the HOLDS answer F-003 does not have
cases.needle: reported `confirmed` while a triage rule HOLDS
cases.why: Three findings here are `confirmed` and every triage rule on them is answered. Answering the rules is not the defect; answering one HOLDS and reporting anyway is.

cases.removes: the family prefix of one of F-002's traceability ids
cases.why: This artifact cites four different families - CWE, API, OWASP and ASVS - and all of them have to be recognised, or the rule is a list of the ones somebody remembered.

cases.removes: the real procedure id on F-002
cases.needle: does not exist in the corpus
cases.why: Every finding here cites a procedure by id. The rule reads the corpus rather than a hardcoded list, so a real id has to survive it.
